To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
as a cell pushes or pulls its nucleus through a narrow constriction, the genomic DNA must distort and somehow maintain integrity despite ever-present double strand breaks.

(i) the DNA in a specific locus engineered in chromosome 1 of a living cell is stretched and aligned as the cell pushes or pulls the nucleus through a small pore; and (ii) this deformation of chromatin is maintained even when the DNA in the locus is cleaved and repair factors recruited.
as a cell pushes or pull its nucleus through a constriction, the submicron chromatin stretches and maintains integrity, even with DNA breaks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how a nucleus deforms when entering a small constriction.
the deformation of chromatin and its ability to maintain genomic integrity during nuclear migration.
understanding the mechanics of chromatin deformation, and the effects of DNA damage and repair on this deformation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chromatin is stretched and maintains continuity in small pores.
the chromatin is able to stretch in a highly organized way, maintaining its integrity and the DNA repair scaffold, even when the DNA is cleaved.
chromatin is highly extended and deformed in a pore and maintains integrity and continuity even with DNA breaks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chromatin is stretched and maintains integrity even with breaks in the DNA.
as a nucleus is pushed through a small pore, chromatin stretches and remains intact, even when the DNA is broken.
chromatin stretches, maintains integrity and repairs breaks, even when the nucleus is pushed into a small pore.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chromatin stretches and maintains integrity as it is pushed into a small pore, even with DNA double strand breaks.
chromatin maintains its structural integrity as it deforms, even when the DNA is cleaved.
chromatin integrity is not compromised during nuclear pore passage, and that DNA damage does not affect chromatin deformation in a small pore.
